build: Production-tagged working tree with pending writing retention, Vim navigation, pane focus and footnote fixes; no performance tuning applied for this profile.

environment.display: Isolated Xvfb 1280x1000x24, GDK X11, software rendering
environment.engine: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Ubuntu; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/60.5 Safari/605.1.15 wails.io/605.1.15

method.input: XTestFakeKeyEvent on an isolated display, native keydown isTrusted checked
method.workload: 560 uniquely numbered paragraphs; 12320 words. Diagram variant inserts 20 identical Mermaid flowcharts (12620 words), one SVG mounted in the typing viewport.
method.settings: All five lens groups versus none; en-US; right pane open throughout; standard editing twice in reverse condition order, Vim Insert once. Default theme, autosave 300 s, automatic commits off.
method.sequence: 70 printable keys per scenario, 60 ms apart for first 50 then a 1.5 s pause and 100 ms intervals. Initial analysis settled before each scenario.
method.metrics: Sender wall clock to keydown (negative sub-ms differences clamped to zero due to Date.now resolution), keydown to native input microtask, keydown to first/second requestAnimationFrame callbacks. Frame callbacks are not completed display presentation.
method.isolation: This retained native run was performed after the Chromium CPU profiler closed. Earlier overlapping exploratory run excluded.
method.limitations: Synthetic native keyboard events; no physical keyboard/compositor/display measurement. Fast Linux desktop, repeated prose patterns, one visible diagram. No Windows/macOS inference. CPU profiling is a separate Chromium devserver run with 500 microsecond sampling; main thread only.
